column1: Does minikube tunnel provision a real cloud load balancer?
column2: No — it simulates one via a network route on your own machine to the cluster's service network; genuinely working EXTERNAL-IP, but not a real cloud load balancer

column1: Why does externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster lose the real client IP?
column2: Cross-node routing requires SNAT'ing the source IP to the receiving node's own address so return traffic can find its way back — the pod only ever sees the node's IP

column1: What's the trade-off of externalTrafficPolicy: Local?
column2: Preserves the real client IP, but traffic to a node with no local matching pod is simply dropped, not forwarded elsewhere
Auto-allocated when externalTrafficPolicy: Local is set on a LoadBalancer Service — lets a real external load balancer learn which nodes have local endpoints, avoiding nodes that would drop traffic

column1: What does sessionAffinity: ClientIP change about Service routing?
column2: Pins a given source IP to the same pod for a configurable window, instead of independently load-balancing every request

column1: Is sessionAffinity cookie-based or IP-based at the plain Service level?
column2: IP-based only — cookie or header-based affinity needs an Ingress controller or service mesh, not available on a plain Service

column1: What's the difference between externalTrafficPolicy and internalTrafficPolicy?
column2: externalTrafficPolicy governs traffic from outside the cluster and controls source-IP preservation via SNAT; internalTrafficPolicy governs pod-to-pod ClusterIP traffic and is purely about reducing cross-node hops, no SNAT concern

column1: When does a Service require named ports?
column2: Once spec.ports[] has more than one entry — every port needs a unique name, or the apply is rejected outright

column1: A NodePort Service with externalTrafficPolicy: Local times out from every single node. What's the likely real cause?
column2: Not the traffic policy itself — check kubectl get endpointslices first; a selector matching zero pods anywhere produces this exact symptom

column1: What's the default timeout for sessionAffinity: ClientIP if sessionAffinityConfig isn't set?
column2: 10800 seconds (3 hours) — a client stays pinned to the same pod for that long since its last request
